title.narrative: Integrated Multi-Sectorial Cholera (WASH Health), Emergency Response for Amhara Region( Bahirdar Zuria, and Bahirdar Town), Ethiopia

description.narrative: ltpgtAs described in the 2025 First Reserve Allocation strategy document at the beginning of 2025, the humanitarian situation in Ethiopia remains critical, driven by a confluence of factors, including ongoing conflicts, particularly in Amhara and western Oromia, back-to-back climate shocks such as La Nina, droughts, floods and landslides, and recurrent health emergencies/cholera. The allocation focuses on scaling up cholera response, in WASH and health services for malnourished children and pregnant and lactating women and ensuring GBV case management in hotspot areas. In Amhara region, the second episode of cholera outbreak started in Bati district (from April 03, 2024, to Apr 7, 2025): a total of 5,874 cases were line-listed with 79 deaths, (CFR 1.34%) were reported the outbreak expanded to 45 districts of 20 zones/City administrations. The GAM rate among children under 5 are 24% which far exceeding the threshold. Meanwhile, the drought has so far displaced over 1,200 people in two deeply impacted zones of North Gondar and Wag Hamra of the Amhara Region. (5) at least 2.4 million livestock face shortage of water and feed in seven zones and nearly 175,000 livestock migrated to neighboring kebeles, in search of water and feed according to the APHI.ltbrgtAt least half of the IDPs in the region are not receiving humanitarian assistance for lack of Government and partners' resource capacities and insecurity. There is delay and shortages of general food distribution (GFD) in IDP sites in North Gondar, North Wello, Wag Hamra, South Wello, Central Gondar and North Shewa zones, where nutrition support is being provided through mobile health and nutrition teams (MHNTs). In response to this crisis, AEID planned to support the cholera epidemic, conflict and drought-affected communities of North Gojjam, Bahirdar Zuria, Andasa Holiy Site, Bahirdar City, in Amhara. The project aims to assist 100,000 individuals through interventions in cholera (WASH and Health) sectors.ltbrgtltbgtHealth Sectorlt/bgt:lt/pgtltpgt1. Support deployment of Kebele Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) in hotspot woredas (briefings, incentives and transport allowance)ltbrgt2. Active case search, supervision and rapid investigation for outbreakprone diseasesltbrgt3. Support Cholera Treatment Centres (CTCs) and Oral Rehydration Points (ORPs), repairs, Infection Prevention and Control (IPC)ltbrgt4. Procurement and distribution of relevant medical supplies to cholera treatment centres and unitsltbrgt5. Multi-stage water quality testing in affected communities and water treatmentltbrgt6. Support to community volunteers for daily house-to-house hygiene promotion in high transmission areasltbrgt7. Support to Oral Cholera Vaccine (OCV) mass campaignltbrgt8. Support to Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) strategylt/pgtltpgtltbgtWASH Sector:lt/bgtltbrgt1. Rehabilitation/expansion/solarization of existing water supply systemsltbrgt2. Construction/maintenance of sanitation facilities at Cholera Treatment Centers (CTC)/communityltbrgt3. Construction of hand washing facilities at CTC/communityltbrgt4. Supply and distribution of WASH supplies and water treatment chemicalsltbrgt5. WASH Social Behavoural Change (SBC)ltbrgtThe project, through a multisectoral approach, aims to reduce the risk of cholera spread among the most vulnerable groups affected by multiple crises. lt/pgt
